A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same dual-task subject-driven video-generation framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-G are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original VBench and OpenS2V evaluations, training ablations, gradient measurements, a human preference study, and motion-stratified temporal evaluation.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds Wan 2.2-5B evaluations, gradient measurements, LoRA-rank experiments, and regularized training comparisons.

M1.justification: The stochastic dual-task schedule, identity conditioning, reference-frame sampling, and token dropping remain intact. v3 adds a Wan 2.2-5B adaptation using flow matching and masked, separate timestep conditioning for reference and video frames (Section 5.1; Appendix A.2), extending rather than replacing the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Subject200K, Pexels videos, the 120-example VBench evaluation, OpenS2V, human preference assessment, and motion-stratified Pexels evaluation. OpenS2V moves from v2 Appendix E.3 to the main text; Wan experiments and additional examples do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Tables 12-13 add L2-regularized and pretrained-weight-anchored variants of image-only and two-stage training as comparison methods. The principal VBench and OpenS2V comparator sets are retained. PCGrad is renamed Gradient Surgery, not introduced as a new comparator.

E3.justification: v3 substantially expands experimental configurations through Wan training with up to 81 frames at 1280×704 and 16 FPS, plus rank sweeps and regularized controls. Section 5.1 also changes the stated LoRA dropout from 0.1 to 0.2. This is a reported setting revision; the PDFs do not establish that retained CogVideoX experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds substantive tests of adapter capacity across ranks 8, 32, 128, and 512 (Appendix D.6), and whether L2 regularization or weight anchoring can remedy image-only and two-stage failures (Appendix D.8). Figure 5 additionally tests gradient behavior on Wan. Existing data-size, switching-probability, PCGrad, and temporal analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain fixed-seed, fixed-validation-batch gradient tracking and the same point-estimate reporting practices. v3 adds no documented repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds Wan benchmark results, gradient traces, qualitative outputs, and numerical rank/regularization results. Wan reports VBench Dynamic Degree 66.67 and DINO-I 60.18, and OpenS2V Total Score 53.26. Retained CogVideoX values remain 69.64, 62.88, and 50.05 respectively; these additions concern a different model configuration, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 Proposition 4.1 asserts expected inner-product convergence under stochastic switching with smooth, locally convex losses. v3 Proposition 4.2.1 narrows this to exponential decay under deterministic mixture-loss gradient descent and local second-order assumptions. This aligns the main statement with the existing Appendix C model; the appendix proofs are essentially retained.

C1.justification: v3 adds explicit cross-backbone transfer claims in the abstract, contributions, and conclusion. The central claims of zero-shot generation without subject-video pairs and adaptation in 288 A100-hours remain. The new '1% compute' emphasis largely reframes efficiency comparisons already present in v2.

C2.justification: v3 explains low-data copy-paste artifacts and why identity metrics can miss them, and adds interpretations of rank and regularization experiments. It qualifies facial-generation limitations using Wan results and mentions rare high-dynamic trajectories, while dropping v2's limitation on arbitrary spatial subject placement. Earlier face-failure examples remain in Appendix G.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds Wan-specific conditioning, resolution, sequence-length, and shared-optimizer information; Section 5.1 revises the documented LoRA dropout. Appendix G newly explains the use of benchmark-provided 14B outputs and their inference-resource requirements. Most CogVideoX reproducibility details and resource-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to SkyReels-V2 and McCloskey and Cohen's catastrophic-interference work, and expands its efficiency positioning against gradient surgery and continual-learning approaches. Most remaining reference changes are publication metadata updates or renumbering of the same works.

P1.justification: v3 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, and explanatory passages around compute efficiency and backbone transfer. It changes terminology, reorganizes implementation details, adds an appendix contents list, and moves OpenS2V and image-data-scaling discussion into the main narrative.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation with widespread resizing and relocation of displays. Wan panels, rank and regularization displays, and ranking colors are added. OpenS2V moves into the main text, PCGrad examples move to the appendix, and face-success and failure displays are separated.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's single-backbone demonstration, v3 strengthens evidence for portability and design choices through Wan results and rank/regularization controls. Its narrower main proposition better matches the existing local proof. These gains support a limited net improvement: new controls omit penalty strengths, Wan positional handling remains underspecified, and the spatial-placement limitation is dropped.
